title: The North Face AI Campaign Thread
thread: The North Face just showed every brand how to use AI for marketing. Here's the play that got them a 340% engagement spike 🧵👇
They used AI-powered social listening to detect a viral TikTok trend — hikers wearing their gear in unexpected urban places. But here's the key: they caught it within HOURS, not the usual days.
Instead of a 3-week campaign approval cycle, they had pre-approved creative frameworks ready. Their team produced responsive content in under 4 hours. Speed isn't reckless when you have systems.

The results:
• 340% increase in social engagement
• 28% lift in DTC sales that week
• 5x more earned media mentions than their planned campaign

This wasn't luck. It was infrastructure.

Why this matters for every brand:

1. AI social listening is now table stakes
2. Pre-approved creative frameworks > approval committees
3. Speed is the new competitive advantage in marketing
The takeaway: The brands winning in 2025 aren't the ones with the biggest budgets. They're the ones with the fastest feedback loops between culture and content.

title: YC Batch AI Analysis Thread
thread: I analyzed every AI company in @ycombinator's latest batch. The patterns tell us exactly where AI is heading 🧵
72% of AI startups are NOT building foundation models. They're building vertical applications on top of existing models. The model layer is consolidating. The opportunity is in the application layer.

The biggest category? Regulated industries.

40% are in healthcare, legal, or finance.

Why? Domain expertise is the moat, not the model. Your competitor can use the same GPT-4 API. They can't replicate your healthcare compliance knowledge.

28% are building developer tools — the picks and shovels play.

Eval frameworks, prompt management, deployment infrastructure.

Every AI application needs tooling. These companies are building the Rails/Django of the AI era.

Only 12% are doing consumer AI. That's telling.

YC's partners are the best pattern-matchers in tech. They're signaling that B2B vertical AI is where the money will be made.

The takeaway for founders:

• Build specific, not general
• Own a vertical, don't compete on the model
• If you're in a regulated industry, your domain knowledge IS your moat
